request_params.Description: A portion of either the family or given name of the patient.

request_params.Name: _id
request_params.Description: The logical ID of the patient.

request_params.Name: family
request_params.Description: A portion of the family (last) name of the patient.

request_params.Name: given
request_params.Description: A portion of the given (first) name of the patient.

request_params.Name: gender
request_params.Description: Patient's gender. M-Male, F-female, O-Other, U-Unknown

request_params.Name: birthdate
request_params.Description: Patient's date of birth.

request_params.Name: identifier
request_params.Description: Patient's identifier. For example, MRN.

response_fields.Name: identifier
response_fields.Description: Patient's identifier. Patients are usually assigned a specific numerical identifier that is unique within the system.

response_fields.Name: active
response_fields.Description: Is the patient's record active? The default value is true. Need to be able to mark a patient record as not to be used because it was created in error. If a record is inactive, and linked to an active record, then future patient/record updates should occur on the other patient.

response_fields.Name: name
response_fields.Description: Name associated with the patient.

response_fields.Name: telecom
response_fields.Description: Patient contact communication detail. This indicates the value in any kind of telecom details field for the patient. If capturing a phone, fax, or similar contact point, the value is a properly formatted telephone number according to ITU-T E.123. However, this is frequently not possible due to legacy data and/or clerical practices when recording contact details. For this reason, phone, fax, page, and email addresses are not handled as formal URLs.

response_fields.Name: gender
response_fields.Description: Patient's gender. Returns Male, Female, Other, or Unknown. For more information on this value set, see Administrative Gender ValueSet.

response_fields.Name: birthDate
response_fields.Description: Patient's date of birth. This indicates a specific calendar date or partial date (either a year or a month and year combination). Time zone is not included. Fuzzy (approximate) dates are not valid.

response_fields.Name: deceasedBoolean
response_fields.Description: Is the patient deceased? If a patient is deceased, it influences the clinical process and human communication. If this value is blank, most systems interpret the missing information as an indication that the patient is alive.

response_fields.Name: address
response_fields.Description: Patient's postal address. Postal addresses are often used to record a location that can be visited to find a patient or person.

response_fields.Name: maritalStatus
response_fields.Description: Patient marital (civil) status. For more information on this value set, see Marital Status Codes.

response_fields.Name: multipleBirthBoolean
response_fields.Description: Was the patient part of a multiple birth?

response_fields.Name: contact
response_fields.Description: Patient's contact party. For example, Guardian, Partner, or Friend).

response_fields.Name: contact.relationship
response_fields.Description: Patient contact's relationship with the patient. For more information on this value set, see patient-contact-relationship.

response_fields.Name: contact.name
response_fields.Description: Patient contact's name.

response_fields.Name: contact.telecom
response_fields.Description: Patient contact's detailed information.

response_fields.Name: contact.address
response_fields.Description: Patient contact's address.

response_fields.Name: communication.language
response_fields.Description: The language used to communicate with the patient about his or her health. For more information on this value set, see Language ValueSet.

response_fields.Name: careProvider
response_fields.Description: Patient's nominated primary care provider.

response_fields.Name: us-core-race
response_fields.Cardinality: 0..1 Patient's race (category of humans sharing history, origin, or nationality). For more information on this value set, see DAF Race ValueSet

response_fields.Name: us-core-ethnicitye
response_fields.Description: Patient's ethnicity (category of humans sharing heritage). For more information on this value set, see Ethnicity group.

response_fields.Name: us-core-religion
response_fields.Description: Patient's professed religious affiliation. For more information on this value set, see v3 Code System ReligiousAffiliation.

request_params.Name: pid
request_params.Description: Patient's logical ID. This is retrieved using the search function.

response_fields.Name: identifier
response_fields.Description: Observation's unique ID. This applies to the instance observation.

response_fields.Name: status
response_fields.Description: Observation's status. Values include Registered, Preliminary, Final, or Amended. For more information on this value set, see observation-status.

response_fields.Name: category
response_fields.Description: Observation's type of classification. For more information on this value set, see observation-category.

response_fields.Name: code
response_fields.Description: Observation's type or code. For more information on this value set, see observation-codes.

response_fields.Name: subject
response_fields.Description: Observation's subject. The patient's (or group of patients) location, or the device whose characteristics (direct or indirect) are described by the observation and into whose record the observation is placed.

response_fields.Name: encounter
response_fields.Description: Observation's encounter. The healthcare event (a patient and healthcare provider interaction) during which the observation is made. For some observations it may be important to know the link between an observation and a particular encounter.

response_fields.Name: effectiveDateTime
response_fields.Description: Clinically relevant time/time-period for observation.

response_fields.Name: effectivePeriod
response_fields.Description: Clinically relevant time/time-period for the observation. The time or time-period the observed value is asserted as being true. For biological subjects (human patients) this is usually called the "physiologically relevant time." This is usually either the time of the procedure or of specimen collection, but very often the source of the date/time is not known, only the date/time itself.

response_fields.Name: issued
response_fields.Description: Date/time the observation was made available. The date and time is typically after the results have been reviewed and verified.

response_fields.Name: performer
response_fields.Description: Individual responsible for the observation.

response_fields.Name: valueCodeableConcept
response_fields.Description: The smoking status. Need to track the status of individual results. Some results are finalized before the whole report is finalized. For more information on this value set, see DAF Smoking Status Value Set.

response_fields.Name: comments
response_fields.Description: Comments about the result.

name: Condition(Problem)
h3_description: Detailed information about conditions, problems, or diagnoses

request_params.Name: pid
request_params.Description: The patient's logical ID. This is retrieved using the search function.

request_params.Name: date
request_params.Description: A string representing a date to include in the search. See below for more information.

response_fields.Name: identifier
response_fields.Description: External ID for the condition. The ID is defined by business processes and/or used to refer to it when a direct URL reference to the resource itself is not appropriate. For example, in CDA documents or in written or printed documentation. This may include IMO, ICD9/10, or Medcin codes.

response_fields.Name: patient
response_fields.Description: Patient name. This indicates the patient who the condition record is associated with. This is used for querying and retrieving patient demographic information.

response_fields.Name: encounter
response_fields.Description: Encounter during which the condition was first asserted.

response_fields.Name: asserter
response_fields.Description: Individual who asserts the condition. This is a provider reference.

response_fields.Name: dateRecorded
response_fields.Description: Date when the condition was first recorded. This is not the date on which the condition was last updated.

response_fields.Name: code
response_fields.Description: ID of the condition, problem, or diagnosis. The value set includes content from SNOMED. For more information on this value set, see condition-code.

response_fields.Name: category
response_fields.Description: Condition category. Valid entries include: Complaint, Symptom, Finding, and Diagnosis. For more information on this value set, see condition-category.

response_fields.Name: clinicalStatus
response_fields.Description: Condition clinical status. Valid entries include: Active, Relapse, Remission, and Resolved. For more information on this value set, see condition-clinical.

response_fields.Name: verificationStatus
response_fields.Description: Condition verification status. Valid entries include: Provisional, Differential, Confirmed, Refuted, Entered-in-error, and Unknown. For more information on this value set, see condition-ver-status.

response_fields.Name: severity
response_fields.Description: Subjective severity of condition. Valid entries include the following SNOMED codes: 399166001 Fatal, 24484000 Severe, 6736007 Moderate, and 255604002 Mild. For more information on this value set, see condition-severity.

response_fields.Name: onsetDateTime
response_fields.Description: Estimated or actual date, date-time, or age when the condition statement was documented. The Date Recorded indicates the date when this particular condition record was created in the EHR, not the date of the most recent update. Onset date is pulled from Problem.OnsetFuzzyWhen.

response_fields.Name: onsetQuantity
response_fields.Description: Estimated or actual date, date-time, or age.

response_fields.Name: onsetPeriod
response_fields.Description: Estimated or actual date, date-time, or age.

response_fields.Name: onsetRange
response_fields.Description: Estimated or actual date, date-time, or age.

response_fields.Name: onsetString
response_fields.Description: Estimated or actual date, date-time, or age.

response_fields.Name: abatementDateTime
response_fields.Description: If/when in resolution/remission.

response_fields.Name: abatementQuantity
response_fields.Description: If/when in resolution/remission.

response_fields.Name: abatementBoolean
response_fields.Description: If/when in resolution/remission.

response_fields.Name: abatementPeriod
response_fields.Description: If/when in resolution/remission.

response_fields.Name: abatementRange
response_fields.Description: If/when in resolution/remission.

response_fields.Name: abatementString
response_fields.Description: If/when in resolution/remission.

response_fields.Name: stage
response_fields.Description: Stage/grade, usually assessed formally.

response_fields.Name: stage.summary
response_fields.Description: Simple summary (disease specific). For more information on this value set, see condition-stage.

response_fields.Name: stage.assessment
response_fields.Description: Formal record of assessment.

response_fields.Name: evidence
response_fields.Description: Supporting evidence.

response_fields.Name: evidence.code
response_fields.Description: Manifestation/symptom. For more information on this value set, see manifestation-or-symptom.

response_fields.Name: evidence.detail
response_fields.Description: Supporting information found elsewhere.

response_fields.Name: bodySite
response_fields.Description: Anatomical location, if relevant. For more information on this value set, see body-site.

response_fields.Name: notes
response_fields.Description: Additional information about the condition.

name: Medications
h3_description: Record of medication being taken by a patient

request_params.Name: pid
request_params.Description: Patient's logical ID. This is retrieved using the search function.

request_params.Name: date
request_params.Description: A string representing a date to include in the search. See below for more information.

response_fields.Name: identifier
response_fields.Description: External identifier. FHIR will generate its own internal identifiers (probably URLs) which do not need to be explicitly managed by the resource. The identifier is one that would be used by another non-FHIR system. For example, an automated medication pump would provide a record each time it operated; an administration while the patient was off the ward might be made with a different system and entered after the event. This is particularly important if these records have to be updated.

response_fields.Name: patient
response_fields.Description: Patient who is or was taking the medication. Defines constraints and extensions on the patient resource for use in querying and retrieving patient demographic information.

response_fields.Name: informationSource
response_fields.Description: The person who provided the information about the taking of this medication.

response_fields.Name: dateAsserted
response_fields.Description: Date and time when the statement was asserted.

response_fields.Name: status
response_fields.Description: Valid entries include: Active, Completed, Entered-in-error, and Intended. For more information on this value set, see medication-statement-status.

response_fields.Name: wasNotTaken
response_fields.Description: Was the medication not taken? True if medication is/was not being taken.

response_fields.Name: reasonNotTaken
response_fields.Description: Instances are not expected or even encouraged to draw from the specified value set. The value set merely provides examples of the types of concepts intended to be included. A code indicating why the medication was not taken. A set of codes indicating the reason why the MedicationAdministration is negated. For example codes, see Reason Medication Not Given Codes. This value set has an inline code system http://hl7.org/fhir/reason-medication-not-given, which defines the following codes: Code "a" - Display "None" - No reason known, Code "b" - Display "Away" - The patient was not available when the dose was scheduled, Code "c" - Display "Asleep" - The patient was asleep when the dose was scheduled, and Code "d" - Display "Vomit" - The patient was given the medication and immediately vomited it back.

response_fields.Name: effectiveDateTime
response_fields.Description: Date and time over which the medication was consumed.

response_fields.Name: effectivePeriod
response_fields.Description: The interval of time during which it is being asserted that the patient was taking the medication (or was not taking, when the wasNotGiven element is true). If the medication is still being taken at the time the statement is recorded, the "end" date will be omitted.

response_fields.Name: note
response_fields.Description: Further information about the statement.

response_fields.Name: supportingInformation
response_fields.Description: Additional supporting information.

response_fields.Name: medicationCodeableConcept
response_fields.Description: The medication that was taken. Defines constraints and extensions on the Medication resource for use in querying and retrieving patient's medication information.

response_fields.Name: medicationReference
response_fields.Description: The medication that was taken.

response_fields.Name: dosage
response_fields.Description: Indicates how the medication is/was used by the patient.

response_fields.Name: dosage.text
response_fields.Description: Reported dosage information.

response_fields.Name: dosage.timing
response_fields.Description: When/how often was medication taken. The timing schedule for giving the medication to the patient. The Schedule data type allows many different expressions. For example, "Every 8 hours," "Three times a day," "1/2 an hour before breakfast for 10 days from 23-Dec 2011," or "15 Oct 2013, 17 Oct 2013 and 1 Nov 2013".

response_fields.Name: dosage.asNeededBoolean
response_fields.Description: Take "as needed" (for x).

response_fields.Name: dosage.asNeededCodeableConcept
response_fields.Description: Take "as needed" (for x).

response_fields.Name: dosage.siteCodeableConcept
response_fields.Description: Where (on body) medication is/was administered. Instances are encouraged to draw from the specified codes for interoperability purposes but are not required to do so to be considered conformant. A coded specification of the anatomic site where the medication first enters the body. This identifies the body site at which the substance was administered. The codes SHOULD be taken from Vaccine Administered Body Site. All codes from system http://snomed.info/sct. The value set includes codes from the following code systems (actual value set has > 1000 codes included): 91723000 - Anatomical structure (body structure), 280115004 - Acquired body structure (body structure), 258331007 - Anatomical site notations for tumor staging (body structure), 118956008 - Altered from its original anatomical structure (morphologic abnormality), or 91722005 - Entire physical anatomical entity (body structure).

response_fields.Name: dosage.siteReference
response_fields.Description: Where (on body) medication is/was administered.

response_fields.Name: dosage.route
response_fields.Description: Route by which the medication entered the body. Instances are encouraged to draw from the specified codes for interoperability purposes but are not required to do so to be considered conformant. Route of Administration value set is based upon FDA Drug Registration and Listing Database (FDA Orange Book) which are used in FDA structured product and labelling (SPL). This value set includes codes as defined in http://ncimeta.nci.nih.gov.

response_fields.Name: dosage.method
response_fields.Description: Technique used to administer the medication.

response_fields.Name: dosage.quantityQuantity
response_fields.Description: Amount administered in one dose.

response_fields.Name: dosage.quantityRange
response_fields.Description: Amount administered in one dose.

response_fields.Name: dosage.rateRatio
response_fields.Description: Identifies the speed with which the medication was or will be introduced into the patient. Typically the rate for an infusion e.g. 100 ml per 1 hour or 100 ml/hr. May also be expressed as a rate per unit of time e.g. 500 ml per 2 hours. Currently we do not specify a default of "�1" in the denominator, but this is being discussed. Other examples: 200 mcg/min or 200 mcg/1 minute; 1 liter/8 hours.

response_fields.Name: dosage.rateRange
response_fields.Description: Dose quantity per unit of time.

response_fields.Name: dosage.maxDosePerPeriod
response_fields.Description: The maximum total quantity of a therapeutic substance that may be administered to a subject over the period of time. For example, 1000mg in 24 hours.

name: Allergy or Intolerance
h3_description: Allergy or intolerance (generally: risk of adverse reaction to a substance)

request_params.Name: pid
request_params.Description: The logical ID of the patient. This is retrieved using the search function.

request_params.Name: date
request_params.Description: A string representing a date to include in the search. See below for more information.

response_fields.Name: identifier
response_fields.Description: Identifier associated with the allergy/intolerance concern that are defined by the business processes and/or used to refer to it when a direct URL reference to the resource is not appropriate. For example, in CDA documents or in written/printed documentation.

response_fields.Name: onset
response_fields.Description: Date and/or time of the onset of the allergy or intolerance.

response_fields.Name: recordedDate
response_fields.Description: Date when the sensitivity was recorded.

response_fields.Name: recorder
response_fields.Description: Individual who recorded the allergy and takes responsibility for its content. Options include either DAF-Practitioner profile or DAF-Patient profile.

response_fields.Name: patient
response_fields.Description: Defines constraints and extensions on the patient resource for use in querying and retrieving patient demographic information.

response_fields.Name: reporter
response_fields.Description: Source of the information about the allergy that is recorded.

response_fields.Name: substance
response_fields.Description: Identification of a substance or class of substances that is considered to be responsible for the adverse reaction risk. AllergyIntolerance.substance has an extensible binding to a value set consisting of: NDF-RT (codes for drug class allergies), RXNORM (codes limited to term types- TTY- such as BN or Brand Name, IN or Ingredient, MIN or multiple ingredient, and PIN or precise ingredient for drug ingredient allergies) or SNOMED CT (used when no other code from the other code systems is appropriate, such as No Known Allergies, No Known Food Allergies, No Known Drug Allergies, or No Known Environmental Allergies). For more information on this value set, see: http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/allergyintolerance-substance-code.

response_fields.Name: status
response_fields.Description: Assertion about certainty associated with the propensity or potential risk of a reaction to the identified substance. The codes shall be taken from the AllergyIntoleranceStatus value set which includes: Active, Unconfirmed, Confirmed, Inactive, Resolved, Refuted, and Entered in Error. Decision support would typically raise alerts for Unconfirmed, Confirmed, and Resolved and ignore a Refuted reaction. In particular, Refuted may be useful for reconciliation of the Adverse Reaction List. Conformance is required and as such, some implementations may choose to make this field mandatory. For more information on this value set, see: http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/allergy-intolerance-status.

response_fields.Name: criticality
response_fields.Description: Estimate of the potential clinical harm or seriousness of the reaction to the identified substance. The codes shall be taken from the AllergyIntoleranceCriticality value set with required conformance and include: CRITL-Low, CRITH-High, and CRITU-Unable to determine. For more information on this value set, see: http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/allergy-intolerance-criticality.

response_fields.Name: type
response_fields.Description: Identification of the underlying physiological mechanism for a reaction risk. This value set includes two types: Allergy or Intolerance. For more information on this value set, see: http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/allergy-intolerance-type.

response_fields.Name: category
response_fields.Description: Category of the allergy. Options include: Food, Medication, Environment, and Other. For more information on this value set, see: http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/allergy-intolerance-category.

response_fields.Name: lastOccurence
response_fields.Description: Date and time of the last known occurrence of the reaction.

response_fields.Name: note
response_fields.Description: Additional text not captured in other fields.

response_fields.Name: reaction
response_fields.Description: Details about each adverse reaction event linked to exposure to the identified substance.

response_fields.Name: reaction.substance
response_fields.Description: Identification of the specific substance considered to be responsible for the adverse reaction event. Note: The substance for a specific reaction may be different from the substance identified as the cause of the risk, but must be consistent with it. For instance, it may be a more specific substance such as a brand medication or a composite substance that includes the identified substance. It must be clinically safe to only process the AllergyIntolerance.substance and ignore the AllergyIntolerance.event.substance. For more information on this value set, see: http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/substance-code.

response_fields.Name: reaction.manifestation
response_fields.Description: Clinical symptoms and signs associated with the event. For more information on this value set, see: http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/manifestation-codes.

response_fields.Name: reaction.description
response_fields.Description: Description of the event as a whole.

response_fields.Name: reaction.onset
response_fields.Description: Date and time when manifestations showed.

response_fields.Name: reaction.severity
response_fields.Description: Severity of the reaction or of the event as a whole. Options include: Mild, Moderate, or Severe. For more information on this value set, see: http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/reaction-event-severity.

response_fields.Name: reaction.exposureRoute
response_fields.Description: How the subject was exposed to the substance. For more information on this value set, see: http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/route-codes.

response_fields.Name: reaction.note
response_fields.Description: Text about the event not captured in other fields.

response_fields.Name: narrative summary

For more information on this value set, see: http://hl7.org/fhir/narrative-status, which defines the following codes: Generated, Extensions, Additional, and Empty.

name: Laboratory Result Observations

request_params.Name: pid
request_params.Description: The logical ID of the patient. This is retrieved using the search function.

request_params.Name: date
request_params.Description: A string representing a date to include in the search. See below for more information.

response_fields.Name: identifier
response_fields.Description: Local ID assigned to the report by the order filler, usually by the information system of the diagnostic service provider. You must know what identifier to use when making queries about this report from the source laboratory and for linking to the report outside FHIR context. Alternate name: ReportID.

response_fields.Name: status
response_fields.Description: Status of the diagnostic report as a whole. Diagnostic services routinely issue provisional/incomplete reports, and sometimes withdraw previously released reports. This is labeled as "Is Modifier" because applications need to take appropriate action if a report is withdrawn. The codes shall be taken from the DiagnosticReportStatus value set, which includes the following statuses: Registered, Partial, Final, Corrected, Appended, Cancelled, and Entered-in-Error. For more information on this value set, see: http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/diagnostic-report-status.

response_fields.Name: category
response_fields.Description: Code that classifies the clinical discipline, department, or diagnostic service that created the report. For example, cardiology, biochemistry, hematology, or MRI. This is used for searching, sorting, and displaying purposes. The level of granularity is defined by the category concepts in the DiagnosticServiceSectionCodes value set. More filtering is performed using the metadata and/or terminology hierarchy in DiagnosticReport.code. Alternate names: Department, Sub-department, service, discipline. Example codes include: AU- Audiology, CH- Chemistry, MB- Microbiology, and HM- Hematology. For more information on this value set, see: http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/diagnostic-service-sections.

response_fields.Name: code
response_fields.Description: Test, panel, or battery that was ordered. The typical patterns for codes are: 1) a LOINC code either as a translation from a "local" code or as a primary code, 2) a local code only if no suitable LOINC exists, or 3) both the local and the LOINC translation. Systems shall be capable of sending the local code if one exists. The codes shall be taken from US Laboratory Observation Profile Observation Name Codes. Other codes may be used where these codes are not suitable. This value set has more than 1000 codes. For more information on this value set, see: http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/report-codes.

response_fields.Name: subject
response_fields.Description: Subject of the report. Usually this is a patient. However, diagnostic services also perform analyses on specimens collected from a variety of other sources.

response_fields.Name: encounter
response_fields.Description: Link to the healthcare event (encounter) when the order was made.

response_fields.Name: effectiveDateTime
response_fields.Description: Specimen Collection Datetime which is the physically relevant dateTime for laboratory tests. If the diagnostic procedure was performed on the patient, this is the time it was performed. If there are specimens, the diagnostically relevant time can be derived from the specimen collection times, but the specimen information is not always available, and the exact relationship between the specimens and the diagnostically relevant time is not always automatic.

response_fields.Name: effectivePeriod
response_fields.Description: Specimen Collection Period which is the physically relevant dateTime for laboratory tests. If the diagnostic procedure was performed on the patient, this is the time it was performed. If there are specimens, the diagnostically relevant time can be derived from the specimen collection times, but the specimen information is not always available, and the exact relationship between the specimens and the diagnostically relevant time is not always automatic. If the start element is missing, the start of the period is not known. If the end element is missing, it means that the period is ongoing, or the start may be in the past, and the end date in the future, which means that period is expected/planned to end at the specified time.

response_fields.Name: issued
response_fields.Description: Date and time that this version of the report was released from the source diagnostic service. Clinicians must be able to check the date that the report was released. This may be different from the update time of the resource itself, because that is the status of the record (potentially a secondary copy), not the actual release time of the report. Alternate names: Date Created, Date published, Date Issued.

response_fields.Name: performer
response_fields.Description: Diagnostic service that is responsible for issuing the report. This is helpful to know who to contact if there are queries about the results. You may need to track the source of reports for secondary data analysis. This is not necessarily the source of the atomic data items. It is the entity that takes responsibility for the clinical report. Alternate names: Laboratory, Service, Practitioner, Department, Company.

response_fields.Name: request
response_fields.Description: Details concerning a test or procedure requested. You need to be able to track completion of requests based on reports issued and also to report what diagnostic tests were requested (not always the same as what is delivered). You need to be able to track completion of requests based on reports issued and also to report what diagnostic tests were requested (not always the same as what is delivered).

response_fields.Name: specimen
response_fields.Description: Details about the specimens on which this diagnostic report is based. If the specimen is sufficiently specified with a code in the test result name, then this additional data may be redundant. If there are multiple specimens, these may be represented per observation or group.

response_fields.Name: result
response_fields.Description: Observations that are part of this diagnostic report. Observations can be simple name/value pairs (for example, "atomic" results), or they can be grouping observations that include references to other members of the group (such as "panels"). You need to support individual results, or report groups of results, where the result grouping is arbitrary, but meaningful. This structure is recursive in that observations can contain observations. Alternate names: Data, Atomic Value, Result, Atomic result, Data, Test, Analyte, Battery, or Organizer.

response_fields.Name: imagingStudy
response_fields.Description: One or more links to full details of any imaging performed during the diagnostic investigation. Typically, this is imaging performed by DICOM enabled modalities, but this is not required. A fully enabled PACS viewer can use this information to provide views of the source images. ImagingStudy and ImageObjectStudy and the image element are somewhat overlapping - typically, the list of image references in the image element will also be found in one of the imaging study resources. However each caters to different types of displays for different types of purposes. Neither, either, or both may be provided.

response_fields.Name: image
response_fields.Description: List of key images associated with this report. The images are generally created during the diagnostic process, and may be directly of the patient, or of treated specimens (for example, slides of interest).

response_fields.Name: image.comment
response_fields.Description: Comment about the image. Typically this is used to provide an explanation for why the image is included, or to draw the viewer's attention to important features. The provider of the report should make a comment about each image included in the report. The comment should be displayed with the image. It would be common for the report to include additional discussion of the image contents in other sections such as the conclusion.

response_fields.Name: image.link
response_fields.Description: Reference to the image source.

response_fields.Name: conclusion
response_fields.Description: Concise and clinically contextualized narrative interpretation of the diagnostic report. You need to be able to provide a conclusion that is not lost among the basic result data. Typically, a report is either [all data, no narrative (e.g. Core lab)] or [a mix of data with some concluding narrative (e.g. Structured Pathology Report, Bone Density)], or [all narrative (e.g. typical imaging report, histopathology)]. In all of these cases, the narrative goes in "text".

response_fields.Name: codedDiagnosis
response_fields.Description: Codes for the conclusion which are SNOMED CT findings codes provided as adjunct diagnosis to the report. The codes should be taken from SNOMED CT Clinical Findings. Included are codes from http://snomed.info/sct where concept is-a 404684003. For more information on this value set, see: http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/clinical-findings.

response_fields.Name: presentedForm
response_fields.Description: Rich text representation of the entire result as issued by the diagnostic service. Multiple formats are allowed but they shall be semantically equivalent. This gives the laboratory the ability to provide its own fully formatted report for clinical fidelity. Note: "application/pdf" is recommended as the most reliable and interoperable in this context.

name: VitalSign

request_params.Name: pid
request_params.Description: The logical ID of the patient. This is retrieved using the search function.

request_params.Name: date
request_params.Description: A string representing a date to include in the search. See below for more information.

response_fields.Name: identifier
response_fields.Description: A unique identifier for the simple observation instance. Allows observations to be distinguished and referenced.

response_fields.Name: status
response_fields.Description: The status of the vital sign result value. The status of individual results needs to be tracked. Some results are finalized before the whole report is finalized. The conformance on this value set is required. Values include: Registered, Preliminary, Final, Amended, Cancelled, Entered in Error, and Unknown. For more information on this value set, see: http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/observation-status

response_fields.Name: category
response_fields.Description: Classification of type of observation. Clinical observations measure the body's basic functions such as such as blood pressure, heart rate, respiratory rate, height, weight, body mass index, head circumference, pulse oximetry, temperature, and body surface area. For more information on this value set, see: http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/observation-category

response_fields.Name: code
response_fields.Description: This identifies the vital sign result type. Coded responses are from C-CDA Vital Sign Results. 1. Shall contain exactly one [1..1] code, where the @code should be selected from ValueSet HITSP Vital Sign Result Type. This value set indicates the allowed vital sign result types. The vocabulary selected for this value set aligns with requirements in the Meaningful Use (MU) Stage 2. Note the concept Blood pressure systolic and diastolic (55284-4) is used to group the related observations Systolic blood pressure (8480-6) and Diastolic blood pressure (8462-4). It shall not be used alone, but both 8480-6 and 8462-2 shall also be valued. The codes shall be taken from C-CDA Vital Sign Result; other codes may be used where these codes are not suitable. For more information on this value set, see: http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/observation-codes

response_fields.Name: subject
response_fields.Description: Who and/or what this vital is for. The patient, or group of patients, location, or device whose characteristics (direct or indirect) are described by the observation and into whose record the observation is placed. Indirect characteristics may be those of a specimen, fetus, donor, other observer (for example a relative or EMT), or any observation made about the subject. Observations have no value if you don't know who or what they're about. Note: One would expect this element to be a cardinality of 1..1. The only circumstance in which the subject can be missing is when the observation is made by a device that does not know the patient. In this case, the observation shall be matched to a patient through some context/channel matching technique, and at this point, the observation should be updated.

response_fields.Name: encounter
response_fields.Description: The healthcare event (for example, a patient and healthcare provider interaction) during which this vital was obtained. For some observations it may be important to know the link between the vital sign and a particular encounter.

response_fields.Name: effectiveDateTime
response_fields.Description: Clinically relevant time/time-period for observation. Often just a dateTime for Vital Signs. Knowing when an observation was deemed true is important to its relevance as well as determining trends. At least a date should be present unless this observation is a historical report.

response_fields.Name: effectivePeriod
response_fields.Description: Clinically relevant time/time-period for observation. Often a dateTime for Vital Signs is preferred but if it is a historical instance, then a time period is sufficient.

response_fields.Name: issued
response_fields.Description: Date/Time this was made available.

response_fields.Name: performer
response_fields.Description: Who is responsible for the observation or obtaining the vital sign. May give a degree of confidence in the observation and also indicates where follow-up questions should be directed.

response_fields.Name: valueQuantity
response_fields.Description: Vital Sign Value recorded with UCUM. Common UCUM units for recording Vital Signs. The codes shall be taken from Common UCUM units as defined in http://unitsofmeasure.org Examples include % (percent), cm (centimeter), kg (kilogram), mm(Hg) (millimeter of mercury), /min (per minute) and kg/m2 (kilogram). Note: Normally, an observation will have either a value or a set of related observations. A few observations (e.g. Apgar score) may have both a value and related observations (for an Apgar score, the observations from which the measure is derived). If a value is present, the datatype for this element should be determined by Observation.code. This element has a variable name depending on the type as follows: valueQuantity, valueCodeableConcept, valueString, valueRange, valueRatio, valueSampledData, valueAttachment, valueTime, valueDateTime, or valuePeriod. (The name format is "�value" + the type name" with a capital on the first letter of the type).

response_fields.Name: valueQuantity.value
response_fields.Description: The value of the measured amount. The value includes an implicit precision in the presentation of the value. Precision is handled implicitly in almost all cases of measurement. The implicit precision in the value should always be honored. Monetary values have their own rules for handling precision (refer to standard accounting text books).

response_fields.Name: valueQuantity.unit
response_fields.Description: A human-readable form of the unit. There are many representations for units of measure and in many contexts, particular representations are fixed and required. For example, mcg for micrograms.

response_fields.Name: valueQuantity.system
response_fields.Description: The identification of the system that provides the coded form of the unit. Need to know the system that defines the coded form of the unit. Fixed value http://unitsofmeasure.org.

response_fields.Name: valueQuantity.code
response_fields.Description: Coded responses from the common UCUM units for vital signs value set. Need a computable form of the unit that is fixed across all forms. UCUM provides this for quantities, but SNOMED CT provides many units of interest. The preferred system is UCUM, but SNOMED CT can also be used (for customary units) or ISO 4217 for currency. The context of use may additionally require a code from a particular system.

response_fields.Name: dataAbsentReason
response_fields.Description: Provides a reason why the expected value in the element Observation.value[x] is missing. Codes specifying why the result (Observation.value[x]) is missing. The codes shall be taken from Observation Value Absent Reason value set, however other codes may be used where these codes are not suitable. This value set contains 9 concepts. For more information on this value set, see http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/observation-valueabsentreason.

response_fields.Name: interpretation
response_fields.Description: This value set defines the set of codes that can be used to indicate the meaning/use of a reference range. The value set is extensible and contains 33 concepts. Examples include A (Abnormal), H (High), L (Low), and N (Normal). For more information on this value set, see http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/observation-interpretation.

response_fields.Name: referenceRange
response_fields.Description: Guidance on how to interpret the value by comparison to a normal or recommended range. Knowing what values are considered "normal" can help evaluate the significance of a particular result. Need to be able to provide multiple reference ranges for different contexts. Most observations only have one generic reference range. Systems may choose to restrict to only supplying the relevant reference range based on knowledge about the patient (for example, specific to the patient's age, gender, weight, and other factors), but this may not be possible or appropriate. Whenever more than one reference range is supplied, the differences between them should be provided in the reference range and/or age properties.

response_fields.Name: — referenceRange.Low
response_fields.Description: Indication that the vital result is lower than the defined reference range. Binding is common UCUM units for recording Vital Signs.

response_fields.Name: — referenceRange.High
response_fields.Description: Indication that the vital result is higher than the defined reference range. Binding is common UCUM units for recording Vital Signs.

response_fields.Name: Respiratory rate
response_fields.Description: Recorded under LOINC Code 9279-1 using UOM of (breaths)/min.

response_fields.Name: Heart rate
response_fields.Description: Recorded under LOINC Code 8867-4 using UOM of (beats)/min.

response_fields.Name: Oxygen saturation
response_fields.Description: Recorded under LOINC Code 59408-5 using UOM of % Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood by Pulse oximetry.

response_fields.Name: Body temperature
response_fields.Description: Recorded under LOINC Code 8310-5 using UOM of Cel or [degF].

response_fields.Name: Body height
response_fields.Description: Recorded under LOINC Code 8302-2 using UOM cm or [in].

response_fields.Name: Body weight
response_fields.Description: Recorded under LOINC Code 29463-7 using UOM g, kg or lb.

response_fields.Name: Body mass index
response_fields.Description: Recorded under LOINC Code 39156-5 using UOM kg/m2.

response_fields.Name: Blood pressure systolic and diastolic
response_fields.Description: Recorded under LOINC Code 55284-4 using UOM mm[Hg].

response_fields.Name: Systolic blood pressure
response_fields.Description: Recorded under LOINC Code 8480-6 using UOM mm[Hg]. When recording a blood pressure using systolic and diastolic as separate entities, both must be recorded in order for the blood pressure to be valid.

response_fields.Name: Diastolic blood pressure
response_fields.Description: Recorded under LOINC Code 8462-4 using UOM mm[Hg]. When recording a blood pressure using systolic and diastolic as separate entities, both must be recorded in order for the blood pressure to be valid.

response_fields.Name: related
response_fields.Description: Codes specifying how two observations are related. This is used when reporting systolic and diastolic blood pressure. The codes shall be taken from the ObservationRelationshipType value set. For more information on this value set, see http://www.hl7.org/fhir/valueset-observation-relationshiptypes.html.

response_fields.Name: subject
response_fields.Description: The person, animal, or group on which the procedure was performed.

response_fields.Name: status
response_fields.Description: in-progress , aborted , completed , entered-in-error. For more information on this value set, see procedure-status.

response_fields.Name: category
response_fields.Description: Classification of the procedure. For more information on this value set, see procedure-category.

response_fields.Name: code
response_fields.Description: Identification code of the procedure. The value set defines a set of codes that can be used to indicate the type of procedure: a specific code indicating type of procedure performed from CPT, SNOMED CT, and ICD10-PCS. For more information on this value set, see procedure-code.

response_fields.Name: notPerformed
response_fields.Description: Was the procedure not performed as scheduled? (Yes if not scheduled.)

response_fields.Name: reasonNotPerformed
response_fields.Description: Reason procedure was not performed. For more information on this value set, see procedure-not-performed-reason.

response_fields.Name: bodySite
response_fields.Description: Target body sites. For more information on this value set, see body-site.

response_fields.Name: reasonCodeableConcept
response_fields.Description: Reason why the procedure was performed.

response_fields.Name: reasonReference
response_fields.Description: Reason for the procedure.

response_fields.Name: performer
response_fields.Description: The individual who performed the procedure. This must be a real person, not equipment.

response_fields.Name: performer.actor
response_fields.Description: Reference to the practitioner.

response_fields.Name: performer.role
response_fields.Description: The role the actor was in. Values come from performer-role.

response_fields.Name: performedDateTime
response_fields.Description: The date/time period over which the procedure was performed. Allows a period to support complex procedures that span more than one date, and also allows for the length of the procedure to be captured.

response_fields.Name: performedPeriod
response_fields.Description: Date/time period during which the procedure was performed.

response_fields.Name: encounter
response_fields.Description: Encounter during which the procedure was performed.

response_fields.Name: location
response_fields.Description: Location where the procedure was performed.

response_fields.Name: outcome
response_fields.Description: The result of procedure. For more information on this value set, see procedure-outcome.

response_fields.Name: report
response_fields.Description: Any report resulting from the procedure.

response_fields.Name: complication
response_fields.Description: Complication following the procedure. For more information on this value set, see condition-code.

response_fields.Name: followUp
response_fields.Description: Instructions for follow up. For more information on this value set, see procedure-followup.

response_fields.Name: request
response_fields.Description: A request for the procedure.

response_fields.Name: notes
response_fields.Description: Additional information about the procedure.

response_fields.Description: Who the care team is for. Identifies the patient whose intended care is handled by the team.

response_fields.Name: status
response_fields.Description: Indicates whether the plan is currently being acted upon, represents future intentions, or is now a historical record. response_fields.Description: Options could include Problem, Health Concern, Care Team, or Assessment and Plan of Treatment. response_fields.Name: participant
response_fields.Description: Members of the team. Identifies all people and organizations who are expected to be involved in the care team. Allows representation of care teams, and helps scope the care plan. In some cases, this may be a determiner of access permissions.

response_fields.Name: participant.role

Roles may be inferred by type of practitioner. These are relationships that hold only within the context of the care team. response_fields.Description: The specific person or organization who is participating in or expected to participate in the care team. name: Goal
h3_description: Intended objective(s) for a patient, group or organization

request_params.Name: pid
request_params.Description: The logical ID of the patient. This is retrieved using the search function.

request_params.Name: date
request_params.Description: A string representing a date to include in the search. See below for more information.

response_fields.Name: identifier
response_fields.Description: External ID for this goal. This is a business identifier, not a resource identifier. This records identifiers associated with this care plan that are defined by business processes and/or used to refer to it when a direct URL reference to the resource itself is not appropriate (for example, in CDA documents, or in written/printed documentation).

response_fields.Name: subject
response_fields.Description: Who the goal is intended for. Subject identifies the patient, group, or organization for whom the goal is being established, typically the patient. Subject is optional to support anonymized reporting.

response_fields.Name: startDate
response_fields.Description: When the goal pursuit begins. A date or partial date (for example, just year or year + month) as used in human communication. There is no time zone. Dates shall be valid dates.

response_fields.Name: startCodeableConcept
response_fields.Description: When the goal pursuit begins. This option is a codable concept that identifies types of events that might trigger the start of a goal as defined in http://snomed.info/sct. For example, Admission to the hospital (32485007), Childbirth (386216000), or Completion time of procedure (442137000).

response_fields.Name: targetDate
response_fields.Description: Reach goal on or before. Indicates either the date or the duration after the start by which the goal should be met. This identifies when the goal should be evaluated. This can be a target date (or partial) or a duration of time.

response_fields.Name: targetQuantity
response_fields.Description: Reach goal on or before. Indicates either the date or the duration after start by which the goal should be met. This identifies when the goal should be evaluated. This can be a target date (or partial) or a duration of time.

response_fields.Name: category
response_fields.Description: Indicates a category the goal falls within, and allows goals to be filtered and sorted based on a particular category. Examples of category include: Treatment, Dietary, or Behavioral. For more information on this value set, see http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/goal-category.

response_fields.Name: description
response_fields.Description: Desired outcome. This is a human-readable description of a specific desired objective of care. Without a description of what's trying to be achieved, the element has no purpose.

response_fields.Name: status
response_fields.Description: Indicates whether the goal has been reached and is still considered relevant. Options include: Proposed, Planned, Accepted, Rejected, In-progress, Achieved, Sustaining, On-hold, and Cancelled. For more information on this value set, see http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/goal-status.

response_fields.Name: statusDate
response_fields.Description: When goal status took effect. This identifies the current status. For example, when the goal was initially created, when the goal was achieved, when the goal was cancelled, and so on.

response_fields.Name: statusReason
response_fields.Description: Captures the reason for the current status. This is typically captured for statuses such as Rejected, On-hold, or Cancelled but could be present for others. Conformance is set as example. For more information on this value set, see: http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/goal-status-reason.

response_fields.Name: author
response_fields.Type: Reference( Patient, Practitioner- https://www.hl7.org/fhir/Practitioner.html or Related Person- https://www.hl7.org/fhir/RelatedPerson.html
response_fields.Description: Who is responsible for creating the goal. This indicates whose goal this is: patient goal, practitioner goal, related person goal, and so on. This is the individual responsible for establishing the goal, not necessarily who recorded it. (For that, use the provenance resource.)

response_fields.Name: priority
response_fields.Description: Identifies the mutually agreed level of importance associated with reaching and/or sustaining the goal. This is used for sorting and presenting goals. Extensions are available to track priorities as established by each participant. For example, priority from the patient's perspective, different practitioners' perspectives, or family member's perspectives. The ordinal extension on coding can be used to convey a numerically comparable ranking to priority. Conformance is preferred and defines the following codes: High, Medium, and Low. Different coding systems may use "low value=important." For more information on this value set, see: http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/goal-priority.

response_fields.Name: addresses
response_fields.Type: Reference(Condition, Observation, MedicationStatement, NutritionOrder, ProcedureRequest, RiskAssessment)
response_fields.Description: Identified conditions and other health record elements that are intended to be addressed by the goal. This allows specific goals to be explicitly linked to the concerns they're dealing with which makes the goal more understandable. Reference profiles include: Condition, Observation, MedicationStatement, NutritionOrder, ProcedureRequest, and RiskAssessment.

response_fields.Name: note
response_fields.Description: Comments or annotation about the goal. Must capture information about the goal that doesn't actually describe the goal. May be used for progress notes, concerns, or other related information that doesn't actually describe the goal itself. This is also an MU requirement, which determines the narrative portion of the goal.

response_fields.Name: outcome
response_fields.Description: The end result of goal. Outcome identifies the change (or lack of change) at the point where the goal was deemed to be cancelled or achieved. Outcome tracking is a key aspect of care planning. Note that this should not duplicate the goal status.

response_fields.Name: outcome.resultCodeableConcept
response_fields.Description: Code or observation that resulted from goal.

response_fields.Name: outcome.resultReference
response_fields.Description: Code or observation that resulted from the goal. This describes what has or has not changed. GoalOutcome: The result of the goal. For example, "25% increase in shoulder mobility," "Anxiety reduced to moderate levels," or "15 kg weight loss sustained over 6 months."

name: Health Concern

request_params.Name: pid
request_params.Description: Patient's logical ID. This is retrieved using the search function.

response_fields.Name: identifier
response_fields.Description: Identifier associated with this condition that are defined by business processes and/or used to refer to it when a direct URL reference to the resource itself is not appropriate. For example, in CDA documents or in written/printed documentation.

response_fields.Name: patient
response_fields.Description: Indicates the patient who the condition record is associated with. This defines constraints and extensions on the patient resource for use in querying and retrieving patient demographic information.

response_fields.Name: encounter
response_fields.Description: Encounter during which the condition was first asserted.

response_fields.Name: asserter
response_fields.Description: Individual who is making the condition statement. This could be a provider or patient reference.

response_fields.Name: dateRecorded
response_fields.Description: Indicates the date when this particular condition record was created in the EHR, not the date of the most recent update in terms of when severity, abatement, and so forth were specified. The date of the last record modification can be retrieved from the resource metadata.

response_fields.Name: code
response_fields.Description: Identification of the condition, problem, or diagnosis. For more information on this value set, see http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/condition-code.

response_fields.Name: category
response_fields.Description: A category assigned to the condition. The categorization is often highly contextual and may appear poorly differentiated or not very useful in other contexts. The value set conformance is preferred and options include: Complaint, Symptom, Finding, and Diagnosis. For more information on this value set, see http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/condition-category.

response_fields.Name: clinicalStatus
response_fields.Description: The clinical status of the condition. The value set conformance is preferred and options include: Active, Relapse, Remission, and Resolved. For more information on this value set, see http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/condition-clinical

response_fields.Name: verificationStatus
response_fields.Description: The verification status of the condition or rather, the verification status to support or decline the clinical status of the condition or diagnosis. The value set conformance is required and options include: Provisional, Differential, Confirmed, Refuted, Entered-in-error, and Unknown. For more information on this value set, see http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/condition-ver-status.

response_fields.Name: severity
response_fields.Description: Subjective severity of condition. The value set conformance is extensible and options include: Fatal, Severe, Moderate, and Mild. Extensions are allowed. For more information on this value set, see http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/condition-severity.

response_fields.Name: onsetDateTime
response_fields.Description: Estimated or actual date, date-time, or age. A date, when the Condition statement was documented. The Date Recorded represents the date when this particular Condition record was created in the EHR, not the date of the most recent update in terms of when severity, abatement, etc. were specified. The date of the last record modification can be retrieved from the resource metadata.

response_fields.Name: onsetQuantity
response_fields.Description: There shall be a code if there is a value and it shall be an expression of time. If system is present, it shall be UCUM. If value is present, it shall be positive. The context of use may frequently define what kind of quantity this is and therefore what kind of units can be used. In this case, it is used to define the onset of the condition.

response_fields.Name: onsetPeriod
response_fields.Description: A time period defined by a start and end date/time. A period specifies a range of times. The context of use will specify whether the entire range applies (for example, "the patient was an inpatient of the hospital for this time range") or one value from the period applies For example, "give to the patient between 2 and 4 pm on 24-Jun 2013."

response_fields.Name: onsetRange
response_fields.Description: A set of ordered Quantity values defined by a low and high limit. A Range specifies a set of possible values; usually, one value from the range applies. For example, "give the patient between 2 and 4 tablets." Ranges are typically used in instructions.

response_fields.Name: onsetString
response_fields.Description: A sequence of Unicode characters to convey the estimated onset of when the condition started.

response_fields.Name: abatementDateTime
response_fields.Description: Estimated or actual date or date-time when the Condition statement was resolved or in remission.

response_fields.Name: abatementQuantity
response_fields.Description: There shall be a code if there is a value and it shall be an expression of time. If system is present, it shall be UCUM. If value is present, it shall be positive. The context of use may frequently define what kind of quantity this is and therefore what kind of units can be used. In this case, it is used to indicate when the condition was resolved or in remission.

response_fields.Name: abatementBoolean
response_fields.Description: There is no explicit distinction between resolution and remission because in many cases the distinction is not clear. Age is generally used when the patient reports an age at which the Condition abated. If there is no abatement element, it is unknown whether the condition was resolved or in remission; applications and users should generally assume that the condition is still valid.

response_fields.Name: abatementPeriod
response_fields.Description: A time period defined by a start and end date/time. A period specifies a range of times for if or when the condition was resolved or in remission.

response_fields.Name: abatementRange
response_fields.Description: A set of ordered quantity values defined by a low and high limit. A range specifies a set of possible values; usually, one value from the range applies. In this case, the range defines if and when the condition was resolved or in remission.

response_fields.Name: abatementString
response_fields.Description: A sequence of unicode characters to convey when the condition was resolved or in remission.

response_fields.Name: stage
response_fields.Description: A set of codified values for which the conformance is example and is typically used to indicate stages of cancer and other conditions. Stage/grade, usually assessed formally. For more information on this value set, see http://hl7.org/fhir/valueset-condition-stage.html.

response_fields.Name: stage.summary
response_fields.Description: A simple summary of the stage such as "Stage 3." The determination of the stage is disease-specific. For more information on this value set, see http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/condition-stage.

response_fields.Name: stage.assessment
response_fields.Description: Reference to a formal record of the evidence on which the staging assessment is based. Reference resources include: ClinicalImpression, DiagnosticReport, and Observation.

response_fields.Name: evidence
response_fields.Description: Supporting evidence or manifestations that are the basis on which this condition is suspected or confirmed. The evidence may be a simple list of coded symptoms/manifestations, references to observations or formal assessments, or both.

response_fields.Name: evidence.code
response_fields.Description: A manifestation or symptom that led to the recording of this condition. This includes a value set where the conformance is examples that describe the manifestations or symptoms. For more information on this value set, see http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/manifestation-or-symptom.

response_fields.Name: evidence.detail
response_fields.Description: Supporting information found elsewhere, such as links to other relevant information, including pathology reports.

response_fields.Name: bodySite
response_fields.Description: Anatomical location, if relevant. This value set includes all the Anatomical Structure SNOMED CT codes. For example, codes with an is-a relationship with 91723000: Anatomical structure. For more information on this value set, see http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/body-site.

response_fields.Name: notes
response_fields.Description: Additional information about the Condition. This is a general note or comment entry for further description of the condition, diagnosis, and prognosis.
